newsitem.title: USA: Senators--use US ag export funds on basic grains.
newsitem.headline: Senators--use US ag export funds on basic grains.

text.p: Three farm-state senators said Friday they opposed use of U.S. export subsidies for wheat flour or malt barley, arguing first priority for the money should be aiding the basic commodities.
In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman, the Plains-state senators also opposed the idea of using export promotion funds to restock disaster-relief grain stockpiles.

"We strongly protest any consideration of using scarce EEP (Export Enhancement Program) funds for exporting value-added products at a time when grain prices received by family farmers (are) precipitously dropping and no EEP assistance has been forthcoming for the basic commodities," they said.
Referring to the idea of tapping EEP and PL-480 Food for Peace funds to restock disaster stockpiles, the senators wrote, "EEP funds should be used to sell American grain, not to store more grain."
The letter was signed by Democrats Byron Dorgan and Kent Conrad of North Dakota and Paul Wellstone of Minnesota.
